title: Real power of a positive real number
statement:
For a real number $x>0$ and a real number $y$, the *power* $x^y\in\mathbf R_{>0}$ is

$$
x^y=\exp(y\log x),
$$

where $\log$ is the natural logarithm on $\mathbf R_{>0}$ and $\exp$ the real exponential. For $y=n\in\mathbf Z$ it is the usual integer power $x^n$, and $x^{y_1+y_2}=x^{y_1}x^{y_2}$, $(x^{y_1})^{y_2}=x^{y_1y_2}$. In this chapter it is used for $q^{w/2}$ with $q$ a prime power and $w\in\mathbf R$ (and $w\in\mathbf Z$ in all uses, where $q^{w/2}=\sqrt{q}^{\,w}$).
